description: In the Bremen System Black builds a solid ...c6 and ...d5 pawn center instead of developing with ...Nc6. White's direct d4 break challenges the pawn duo head-on, leading to Caro-Kann-like structures with reversed colors where understanding pawn breaks matters more than memorization.

lines.description: After 1.c4 e5 2.Nc3 Nf6, White chooses the immediate fianchetto 3.g3 and Black sets up with 3...c6, preparing ...d5. White develops 4.Bg2 and Black occupies the center with 4...d5. After 5.cxd5 cxd5, White strikes at once with 6.d4, challenging Black's central duo before it becomes entrenched. The resulting isolated-pawn and hanging-pawn structures reward active piece play from both sides.
